findings.title: Permit FULL checkpoint fallback when the selected policy lowers the depth bound
findings.description: BeginBuild passes the new command.max_delta_depth to both _load_chain and reconstruct before storage_plan can choose FULL. A valid SEALED parent created under a prior immutable policy can have depth greater than a newly activated policy's bound. For example, a valid depth-1 parent under bound 1 and a new policy bound 0 should produce a depth-0 FULL checkpoint, as storage_plan(parent, 0) already specifies. Instead BeginBuild rejects the chain before reaching that fallback. A normal stricter-policy transition therefore cannot compact the provided canonical parent, contrary to the packet's policy-bound FULL fallback and logical DB section 8.2.
findings.reproduction: A read-only Python probe constructed and digest-validated a SEALED FULL plus depth-1 SEALED DELTA under max_depth=1. reconstruct(parent, ancestors, max_depth=1) succeeded and storage_plan(parent, 0) returned ('FULL', None, 0). A CanonicalViewService subclass replaced only _guard and _load_chain with read-only fixture access; invoking the actual begin_build with parent_id set and max_delta_depth=0 raised FactsetError('invalid chain depth/mode') before database access or FULL fallback. The real _load_chain additionally rejects the ancestor traversal at that smaller limit.
findings.requested_change: Validate and reconstruct the historical SEALED parent with its own immutable captured policy bound, then apply the newly selected policy bound to storage_plan and the resulting new build. Preserve bounded traversal and all existing closed-chain checks. Add a meaningful regression for a policy decrease, including parent depth greater than the new limit, proving a FULL checkpoint preserves the ordered membership, complete basis, digest and count and remains sealable under the new policy.
